cells.tense: Present tense — here, with the pen.
cells.verb: You're refining what you can see in private — sorting what matters from what doesn't before anyone has asked you to speak.
cells.place: You're tending something that hasn't taken its full shape yet, letting it develop without forcing the moment.
cells.ask: Offer one more patient pass than feels necessary. Friendship with time is the next thing this care is free to feed.
cells.core: You're doing the careful thinking under the surface, and it's working. The distinctions you're making in private are real, and they're making your tending more precise, not less generous. You can already tell what this growing thing needs next; you're just not rushing it into the open before it's ready.
cells.sheetLine: You're sorting what matters in private, and it's making your care more precise.

cells.tense: Future tense — bracing at a future that can't be written in.
cells.verb: You're refining past the point anyone asked — checking again, tightening again, trying to be ready for a moment that hasn't arrived.
cells.place: You're running ahead of what you're caring for, forcing an outcome it isn't ready to give you yet.
cells.ask: Say it once to someone who can hear it, and let their acknowledgement land. Let one thing finish before you pick up the next — the completion you're avoiding is the release you actually want.
cells.core: You're examining what's growing like it could fail if you look away. The refinement keeps multiplying because somewhere ahead is a version where you finally got it right — and every pass becomes another chance to prove it. You're spending the care on control, and the thing you're trying to grow can feel the difference.
cells.sheetLine: You're refining past the point of usefulness, trying to force a moment that hasn't come.

cells.tense: Past tense — still standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.verb: You stopped sorting — the careful attention that used to tell you what mattered has gone quiet, and you've been letting it.
cells.place: You're caring for something from a distance, giving it less than it needs while you wait for a door that already closed.
cells.ask: Let something come back to you from one person you've been giving to. Exchange, not effort, is what refills care that's been running on empty.
cells.core: There was a point where the private work didn't seem to land, and you took that as a verdict on the work. So you stopped. The care is still there, but it's running thin — and the thinning isn't about the thing you're growing, it's about what you stopped giving back to yourself. Someone nearby would trade with you if you'd let them.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped sorting, and the care has been running thin ever since.

cells.tense: Disowned present — pen down in a room you're already writing.
cells.verb: You're already sorting what matters from what doesn't — the refinement is running every day, and you call it 'just noticing'.
cells.place: You're already creating the conditions for this to grow — the patience, the timing, the attention — and you'd say it's growing itself.
cells.ask: Name one thing you imagined for what you're tending and haven't admitted you want. The satisfaction you're looking for is already in the picture — you just haven't claimed it.
cells.core: You already know what you see, and you already know what it could become — you've been imagining the finished thing for a while. But you talk about the care like it doesn't belong to you, like the growth is happening on its own. The vision is yours. The shaping is yours. The credit is sitting unclaimed in the room you're already in.
cells.sheetLine: You're already shaping what's growing. You just haven't claimed the shaping.
